analysis.one_liner: Vedanta Ltd is now the 'residual' post-demerger entity centred on a ~63% stake in Hindustan Zinc plus its own zinc-international, copper and ferro-chrome operations, after its aluminium, power, oil & gas, and iron & steel businesses were spun off into four separately listed companies in 2026.
analysis.whats_happening: Vedanta's board declared a first FY27 interim dividend of Rs 5/share on 8 Oct 2026 (record date 14 Oct 2026). On 3 Oct 2026 it released Q2 FY27 (July-Sept) production numbers: record quarterly zinc and chrome output, but Copper International sales volumes fell 74% YoY because of shipping disruption linked to the Strait of Hormuz closure. Formal Q2/H1 FY27 financial results are still awaited and should land within the next couple of weeks - the insider trading window stays closed until then.
analysis.plain_terms: In May 2026 Vedanta split into five companies: shareholders kept their original shares (now a smaller, zinc-and-copper-focused business) plus got one new share each in the spun-off aluminium, power, oil & gas, and iron-and-steel companies. That is why the share price looks like it 'crashed' from a peak of Rs 772 to Rs 246 - most of that drop is value that moved into four other listed shares, not value destroyed. The real open question is narrower: is this smaller zinc/copper business, on its own, actually cheap, and can you trust that its controlling family has pledged almost its entire stake to secure group debt.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026) showed PAT attributable to owners of Rs 5,473 crore (+71.8% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 8,501 crore (+98.8% YoY), with margin expanding from 27.1% to 35.1%. Caution: these figures straddle the demerger (effective 1 May 2026) and some reports quote a different, larger PAT growth figure (152%) measured on a different profit line - the two percentages are not interchangeable, and management itself has flagged the comparability issue around the split. Q2 FY27 (not yet fully reported) showed record zinc/chrome volumes but a 74% drop in copper sales volumes due to a logistics disruption, not a demand problem.
analysis.performance_read: Reported returns show the stock down 46.7% over 1 year versus Nifty -9.5% and peer Hindalco +17%, but 3-year (+34.2% vs Nifty +16.8%, peer +90.9%) and 5-year (+31.4% vs Nifty +25.3%, peer +73%) returns are positive. These figures need a large corporate-action caveat: the stock peaked at Rs 772 in April 2026 right before the demerger, and the ~Rs 300-325 'fair value' analysts assigned to the residual entity immediately after the split implies roughly 55-60% of that peak value was distributed to shareholders as shares in the four new companies, not lost. If the return series above is based on raw price alone (unclear from the data supplied) rather than adding back the value of those four new shares, the 1-year and possibly longer-period returns are understated. Separately, the stock has still fallen from that ~Rs 300-325 post-demerger level to today's Rs 246 (a fresh 52-week low) - a real, additional decline of roughly 20-25% in the residual business itself, over and above the demerger adjustment, which is the part investors should actually be worried about.
analysis.valuation_read: Third-party screens show a P/E near 3.4x and P/B near 1.9x (book value ~Rs 127/share). A single-digit P/E this low for a metals company is unusual enough that it is likely distorted by one-off, demerger-related gains sitting in trailing EPS rather than reflecting sustainable earnings power - this needs checking against Screener's own adjusted/standalone figures before being read as 'cheap'. P/B of ~1.9x is a more stable yardstick and is not screamingly cheap. Why it might look cheap: market uncertainty right after a complex five-way split, the copper shipping disruption, and the promoter-pledge overhang. Whether it is actually cheap cannot be answered confidently until normalised, post-demerger earnings settle over a couple of quarters.
analysis.growth_read: Mixed and genuinely volume-led in the core business: Zinc India posted record Q2 and H1 FY27 mined-metal output (271kt in Q2, +5% YoY; 539kt in H1, +3% YoY), and Zinc International commissioned Gamsberg Phase 2. Copper volumes collapsed (-74% YoY) but due to an external shipping disruption (Strait of Hormuz), not weak demand, so it should not be read as a structural decline. The EBITDA margin jump to 35.1% was helped by higher metal prices and a lighter, smaller post-demerger company rather than by volume alone.
analysis.health_read: At the VEDL level, balance-sheet risk looks low: net debt of Rs 8,299 crore and Net Debt/EBITDA of just 0.3x as of June 2026, per the company's own disclosure - among the lowest in the sector, helped by shedding the more debt-heavy aluminium, power and oil & gas units. The real financial risk sits one level up: parent Vedanta Resources (UK) is mid-way through a ~$5.2 billion debt refinancing and has been repeatedly raising bonds, and the promoter group has pledged essentially its entire 54.72% VEDL stake to secure one such bond. So the business itself converts profit to cash reasonably well; the risk to watch is leverage and cash demands at the promoter/parent level flowing down to VEDL.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 54.72% (down from 56.4% pre-demerger in March 2026, largely a mechanical effect of the split rather than an active sell-down). As of 18 September 2026, promoter group entities had created an encumbrance (pledge) over that entire 54.72% stake to secure a $100 million bond issued by Vedanta Resources Finance II - a significant, recurring pattern of using VEDL shares as collateral for group debt, and worth flagging prominently. FIIs hold about 15.8% and domestic institutions about 10.8% (mutual funds ~5.1%); LIC has historically been a holder (~4.5% as of mid-2026, not independently reconfirmed for the latest quarter - check current filings). No globally recognised marquee investor (e.g., a well-known global fund with a headline stake) turned up in available sources - worth noting plainly rather than assuming one exists.
strengths: Zinc India delivered record Q2 and H1 FY27 mined-metal output (271kt in Q2, +5% YoY; 539kt H1, +3% YoY) - genuine volume growth in the core business
EBITDA margin expanded from 27.1% to 35.1% YoY in Q1 FY27, aided by higher metal prices and a leaner post-demerger structure

Net debt of Rs 8,299 crore with Net Debt/EBITDA of just 0.3x (company disclosure, June 2026) - a much lighter balance sheet after shedding the capital-intensive aluminium, power and oil & gas businesses
TTM dividend of Rs 16/share (6.5% yield) with a fresh Rs 5/share interim declared for FY27 in October 2026, continuing a steady payout habit
watchpoints: Promoter group has encumbered essentially its entire 54.72% stake (disclosed 18 Sept 2026) to secure a $100 million group bond - a recurring reliance on pledging VEDL shares for parent-level debt
Copper International sales volumes fell 74% YoY in Q2 FY27 due to Strait of Hormuz-related shipping disruption - watch whether this resolves or becomes a recurring logistics drag

Reported P/E (~3.4x) and ROE (~36.7%) look unusually distorted for a metals company and may include demerger-related one-off gains - verify against Screener's standalone/adjusted figures before treating the stock as statistically cheap

Stock has fallen a further ~20-25% from its post-demerger indicative value (~Rs 300-325 in May 2026) to today's Rs 246, a fresh 52-week low - a real decline specific to the residual business, separate from the demerger-driven price reset
analysis.one_thing: The formal Q2 FY27 (quarter and half-year ended 30 September 2026) financial results, due within roughly the next two weeks, will show whether the copper shipping disruption is temporary noise or a deeper margin issue in the newly slimmed-down entity.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 results and demerger structure were cross-checked across Business Standard, Upstox, Finology, Scanx and ICICI Direct and are consistent. Screener-sourced P/E (3.38x) and ROE (36.71%) could not be independently verified and may reflect non-recurring demerger-related items - treat as 'not verified, check on Screener' pending the next quarter's clean numbers. Secondary aggregators show a conflicting 52-week range (e.g., Rs 174.97-360, likely on a demerger-adjusted/rebased basis) versus the supplied verified range (Rs 245.9-772.14, raw); the supplied verified figures were treated as authoritative per source-priority rules, and the discrepancy is attributed to differing demerger-adjustment methodology rather than averaged.
